subject: Fraud & Scams
title: The Sunk Cost Trap
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Sunk Cost Trap usable.

hook.text: You've invested $50,000 and something feels wrong. Do you pull out or put in more?

buildup.text: Most people invest more. Pulling out means accepting the loss — and that feels unbearable.

discovery.text: This is the sunk cost fallacy: the more you've invested, the harder it is to walk away.

twist.text: Ponzi operators know this. They encourage 'doubling down' when victims start having doubts.

climax.text: Victims who could have lost a little end up losing everything because they couldn't accept a small loss.

punchline.text: Cutting losses early is painful. Not cutting them is worse.

quiz.question: What is the sunk cost fallacy?
options: Continuing because you've already invested too much to quit
